ui.brandSubtitle: Interactive LP · MIP · QP · CP · SMT Exercises (WaSHI & PuLP)
ui.aboutBody: Knowing optimization algorithms at a high level is rarely enough to develop an instinct for translating a problem into variables and constraints—or diagnosing why a model turns out INFEASIBLE. This 100-exercise drill lets you write models directly in the browser without local setup and practice core formulation patterns across LP, MIP, convex QP, CP, and SMT with automated grading.

aboutPoints.label: Zero-setup automated grading
aboutPoints.body: Run your model in-browser with WebAssembly solvers (HiGHS and others) and verify constraint violations (VIOLATION), optimality (SUBOPTIMAL), and infeasibility (INFEASIBLE).

aboutPoints.label: Formulation notes for every exercise
aboutPoints.body: Each exercise includes the mathematical model and implementation notes explaining why those variables and constraints are chosen.

aboutPoints.label: PuLP (Python) runtime alongside WaSHI
aboutPoints.body: While WaSHI itself is a TypeScript / JavaScript library (not a Python package), Pyodide runs PuLP backed by HiGHS in the browser so Python practitioners can work through the same exercises and compare idioms side by side.

aboutPoints.label: AI-generated exercises with ongoing review
aboutPoints.body: Exercises and editorials are generated with generative AI (Gemini), verified against automated solver checks, and reviewed iteratively by hand (reviewed exercises display "Reviewed by ..."). Finalized exercises also link to dedicated GitHub Discussions threads for questions and feedback.

1.title: Modeling Basics — Variables, Constraints & Objective
1.description: Learn step by step how to turn plain problem descriptions into decision variables, linear inequalities, 0-1 binary choices, multi-period inventory flow, and mixed-integer linking constraints.

2.title: MIP Formulation Idioms — Logic, Big-M & Set Covering
2.description: Semi-continuous lots, fixed-charge networks, cardinality and logical Big-M constraints, set covering/partitioning, multidimensional knapsack, piecewise discounts, and facility location.

3.title: Linearization Idioms & LP Duality / Sensitivity
3.description: Minimax epigraphs, L1 deviations, positive-part penalties, Charnes-Cooper ratio linearization, binary product linearization, tight Big-M, shadow prices, and reduced costs.

4.title: Constraint Programming (CP / LCG) & Global Constraints
4.description: AllDifferent (distinct), Element (at), Table (allowed), NoOverlap (disjoint), Cumulative scheduling, 2D packing, symmetry breaking, and MIP vs CP comparison.

5.title: Propositional Logic, SMT & Conflict Diagnosis
5.description: Uniqueness proofs via no-good cuts, logic refutation, dependency & policy verification, minimal Unsat Core extraction, MaxSAT repair, historical audits, and SMT-LIRA.

6.title: Networks, Total Unimodularity, Connectivity & Vehicle Routing
6.description: Exploit total unimodularity, max-flow min-cut, resource-constrained paths, flow-based connectivity without subtours, TSP, CVRP, VRPTW, and connected territory design.

7.title: Production, Inventory, Supply Chain & Energy Systems
7.description: Strong lot-sizing reformulations, multi-item CLSP, backorders vs lost sales, multi-level BOM/MRP, cross-docking, Unit Commitment, and battery arbitrage.

8.title: Scheduling, Staff Rostering, Timetabling & Allocation
8.description: Tardiness & setup-dependent scheduling, job-shop (MIP vs CP), RCPSP, rolling night-rest rosters, skill & pair constraints, university timetabling, and OR slot allocation.

9.title: Multi-Objective Tradeoffs, Fairness, Rescheduling & Uncertainty
9.description: Elastic soft hierarchies, lexicographic tradeoffs, Pareto curves, fairness metrics (including quadratic balancing), Hamming-distance rescheduling, stochastic recourse, CVaR, and robust optimization.

10.title: Strengthening, Decomposition & Hybrid Solver Architecture
10.description: Tighter Big-M & scaling, cover/symmetry cuts, iterative subtour cuts, cutting-stock & routing column generation, Dantzig-Wolfe, classical & logic-based Benders, LNS, and S&OP synthesis.
